title: Prime Number Generator
story: Prime numbers are the atoms of mathematics — every number is built from them. Generating primes was one of the first 'real' programs ever written. Build your own prime sieve and watch the fundamental building blocks of arithmetic appear.
why: Generating primes combines Vec for storage, while loops for iteration, and the prime-checking algorithm in a complete, useful program.
analogy: Prime numbers are like the periodic table of elements for math. Just as every molecule is a combination of atoms, every number is a product of primes. Your prime generator is the 'element discoverer' — finding these atomic building blocks one by one.
try_it: Modify the generator to also count how many divisibility checks it made. Compare the 'check all primes' approach vs 'check up to sqrt(n)' — how many checks are saved? Try generating 100 primes and printing only every 10th one.
tips: Skip checking divisors beyond sqrt(n) — if no divisor found by then, it's prime
Even numbers > 2 are never prime — skip them to cut checks in half
Store found primes in a Vec to reuse them when checking later candidates
common_mistakes: Forgetting that 1 is NOT prime — start checking from 2
Checking divisibility by EVERY number instead of only primes
Not breaking early when a divisor is found
